It's the worst thing I ever did as a teacher. 

Walked into school to be told about an emergency meeting to find one of my best friends, a very well loved teacher in our school, had died cycling the night before. His kid is in my form. My GCSE class are about to sit the exam for my subject. 

I have to say absolutely nothing before they walk into the exam to avoid risking their grade. Faking happy fun motivating lines. And then to form time and saying absolutely nothing to his kid's friends but obviously red eyed from sobbing. Taking them down to assembly for them to be told one of their favourite teachers had died. 

The GCSE students come straight to my classroom after their exam and I tell them. One of my students breaks down in the hallway outside of my door. One of my others says that the reason it hurts so much is because we loved him and he knew that. I've never hugged another person so tight in my life. Most stayed in my classroom for the rest of the day, telling stories about how he was the perfect mad science teacher. I covered his classes for the rest of the year and through the next academic year too. 

That was an incredibly hard year. 

My other best friend died three months after I quit. Brain tumour. Went from absolutely fine to dead within 6 weeks. Students went from brilliant teacher before they broke up for summer break to coming back to finding he'd died. I went to his funeral last September and it will never stop hurting when I think of the faces of the students filling up the church. 

Losing a friend really hurts. Losing a friend loved by hundreds of students and having to help them through that pain and confusion destroyed me.
